newsitem.title: New Zealand: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - March 11.

text.p: Up to $2 million in funding is alleged to be unaccounted for in a battle for control of Levin's Mua-Upoko tribe. A large group of elders is trying to wrest control of the tribe from a tribal authority that they say has been active for 11 years without reporting fully to members or presenting annual financial accounts. But the Mua-Upoko runanga (authority) says it has made regular reports to members and that the disputed funding amounts to $900,000. It says it will fight to keep control. Page 1.

A furious Jim Anderton on Monday said NZ First leader Winston Peters "obvious was in worse shape than I thought" during last Wednesday night's fracas after Peters claimed on Sunday that the Alliance leader was not present. Anderton has laid a complaint with Speaker Doug Kidd. Kidd will forward it to Parliament's privileges committee today if he thinks evidence exists that Parliament's rules were breached during the incident. Peters has admitted he had been drinking beforehand.

Negotiators working out the detail of government policy to provide free healthcare for children up to five are confident of July 1 implementation covering everything except, perhaps, very late-night emergencies. Phil White, spokesman for the four regional health authorities, said research done by the General RHA showed that 90 percent of children's visits to the doctor were between 8am and 5pm on weekdays. Page 2.

Labour education spokesman Trevor Mallard had misrepresented the facts about government funding for private schools, Independent Schools Council executive director Jan Kerr said on Monday. On Saturday Mallard said that government subsidies for private schools totalled $18.9 million in 1996, an increase of 400 percent since 1990. Kerr said the Labour government had reduced funding and many independent schools had had to integrate with the state system in 1990 and 1991. Page 2.

Former press gallery journalist and public relations consultant Roger Foley has been appointed chief press secretary to Deputy Prime Minister and NZ First Leader Winston Peters. Foley, 46, who has just returned from 18 months of sailing around the Pacific, said it was his fourth time at Parliament. On Monday, he gave a strict "no comment" to questions about Peters's late-night fracas last Wednesday with National MP John Banks. Page 2.

Fletcher Challenge Canada will gain more than C$600 million (NZ$623 million) from the sale of its 52 percent stake in TimberWest Forest, announced on Monday. After the announcement, shares in parent Fletcher Paper jumped 13 cents to close at $3.09, with more than two million shares traded. Fletcher Paper owns 50.8 percent of Fletcher Challenge Canada. Page 14.

Hellaby Holdings has acquired a 38.25 percent stake in R Hannah and Co. The diversified investment group has obtained the holding by exercising a previously announced option to buy 51 percent of Hannahs. Following this it has on-sold a 12.5 percent
stake and $1.25 million of subordinated secured debt in the footwear retailer to Hannahs chief executive Michael Beagley.

Qantas looks to set secure Air New Zealand's half stake in Australia's biggest travel retailer and wholesaler, Jetset, though a series of share swaps. Air New Zealand confirmed on Monday that due diligence was being done on the stake that lost the airline $8.019 million in the last financial year and $3.11 million in the previous year. Prices touted in Australia for the stake swing from A$15 million ($16.8 million) to A$50 million.

Richina Pacific is making a $34 million cash issue to retire debt and have cash on hand for new investments, particularly for aquarium-entertainment complexes in Asia. The one-for-two capital raising issue at 30 cents a share was announced on Monday at the same time Richina Pacific reported significantly improved results for the six months to December, $1.272 million ($228,000 in the previous period). The balance date was changed last year so the previous six-month figure is not audited. Page 14.

Resolute Resources, with Dominion Gold Operations, has signed a joint venture with the aboriginal Maralinga Tjarutja people to explore freehold land owned by the Maralinga Tjarutja. The deal will see the Maralinga company MT Mining acquire a 10 percent free carried interest in the joint venture, but MT Mining will have to pay its share of any development costs if mining proceeds. Page 14.

Concrete maker Milburn New Zealand has reported a 6.6 percent rise in net profit to $24.29 million for the year to December 31. The result, which includes a $4.94 million equity-accounted loss on the company's Chinese investments -- up from $2.5 million previously -- was achieved on a 9.6 percent rise in sales revenue to $186.78 million. Pre-tax operating profits were up 15.7 percent at $49.89 million, with the bottom-line result trimmed by tax of $17.57 million and $3.08 million in minority interests. Page 14.
